subject: Preferably Preserved Status for 31 South Street
overview: The Commission designated 31 South Street as preferably preserved to protect neighborhood character and voted to find 7 Hamlin Avenue not historically significant. The meeting also included discussions on renaming the 'Slave Wall' at Thomas Brooks Park to honor its enslaved builder and addressed budget constraints affecting historic survey grants.

items.title: 31 South Street Demolition Hearing
items.summary: The property was found to be preferably preserved following a discussion on its architectural integrity and neighborhood context; the owner expressed a willingness to work with the commission on design modifications.

items.title: 7 Hamlin Avenue Significance Hearing
items.summary: The commission found the property not historically significant because it lacked sufficient architectural integrity and compelling social history, allowing the project to proceed.

items.title: 28 Grove Street Demolition Application
items.summary: The commission accepted the demolition application and approved $500 for a Form B historical survey.

items.title: 91 Winchester Street Carriage House Application
items.summary: The commission accepted the demolition application for the carriage house and approved $500 for a Form B survey.

items.title: Routine Business and Minutes
items.summary: The commission noted no update on the annual report and approved the meeting minutes for December 2022.

items.title: Fieldstone Wall and Pomp's Wall Project
items.summary: Commissioners discussed mobilizing the restoration of the Fieldstone wall and initiating a community process to rename the 'Slave Wall' to 'Pomp's Wall' to humanize its enslaved builder.

items.title: Historic Survey Projects and Budget Issues
items.summary: The commission reviewed a $18,000 budget shortfall and municipal finance constraints that prevent grant funds from rolling over between fiscal years, threatening current survey projects.
